root_cause.text: The netfilter NAT registration/unregistration paths freed `nf_nat_core.c`’s dynamically allocated hook-op wrappers and `priv` objects immediately with `kfree()`, even though those structures can remain reachable by hook-dump/exposition code after registration or during teardown, creating a use-after-free race.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `kfree(ops)`/`kfree(nat_ops)` with `kfree_rcu(...)` in `iptable_nat.c`, `ip6table_nat.c`, and `nf_nat_core.c`, and changes the error path in `nf_nat_register_fn()` to free each `nat_ops[i].priv` via `kfree_rcu(priv, rcu_head)`; the commit message explicitly says the bug appears because userspace hook dumping “will peek back into the nf_hook_ops” and that NAT ops “have to be deferred too.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The netfilter NAT registration/unregistration paths freed `nf_nat_core.c`’s dynamically allocated hook-op wrappers and `priv` objects immediately with `kfree()`, even though those structures can remain reachable by hook-dump/exposition code after registration or during teardown, creating a use-after-free race.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `kfree(ops)`/`kfree(nat_ops)` with `kfree_rcu(...)` in `iptable_nat.c`, `ip6table_nat.c`, and `nf_nat_core.c`, and changes the error path in `nf_nat_register_fn()` to free each `nat_ops[i].priv` via `kfree_rcu(priv, rcu_head)`; the commit message explicitly says the bug appears because userspace hook dumping “will peek back into the nf_hook_ops” and that NAT ops “have to be deferred too.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use RCU-safe freeing for `ops` in the registration error path to prevent premature deallocation and potential races.
intent_record.what: In the error path of `ipt_nat_register_lookups(struct net *net)`, the cleanup call for `ops` was changed from `kfree(ops);` to `kfree_rcu(ops, rcu);`.
intent_record.how: Instead of freeing the lookup operations array immediately, the memory is now released after an RCU grace period. This avoids use-after-free races if other readers may still access `ops` under RCU protection during or after partial registration cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer freeing NAT lookup ops with RCU to avoid use-after-free during unregister.
intent_record.what: In `ipt_nat_unregister_lookups(struct net *net)`, the cleanup call at the end of the function changed from `kfree(ops);` to `kfree_rcu(ops, rcu);`.
intent_record.how: The `ops` object is no longer freed immediately when the unregister function runs; instead, it is released after an RCU grace period, preventing use-after-free if other readers may still access it through RCU-protected paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use RCU-safe freeing for `ops` in the registration failure path to avoid premature deallocation and potential use-after-free.
intent_record.what: In the error path of `ip6t_nat_register_lookups()`, the code changes the cleanup of `ops` from `kfree(ops);` to `kfree_rcu(ops, rcu);`.
intent_record.how: Instead of freeing the allocated `ops` array immediately after unregistering previously registered functions, the memory is now released after an RCU grace period. This prevents use-after-free if any readers can still access `ops` via RCU-protected references during or shortly after rollback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer freeing the nat lookup ops array with RCU to avoid premature deallocation and possible use-after-free.
intent_record.what: In ip6t_nat_unregister_lookups(), the call to free the local ops array was changed from kfree(ops) to kfree_rcu(ops, rcu).
intent_record.how: This defers reclamation of the ops memory until after an RCU grace period, preventing use-after-free if other readers can still access the array during concurrent RCU-protected lookups or callbacks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the nf_nat registration failure cleanup to free NAT hook data safely with RCU instead of immediate kfree().
intent_record.what: In the error path after nf_register_net_hooks() fails, the code no longer frees each nat_ops[i].priv and nat_ops directly with kfree(); it now assigns each priv pointer to a local variable and frees it with kfree_rcu(priv, rcu_head), and frees nat_ops with kfree_rcu(nat_ops, rcu).
intent_record.how: This changes cleanup on registration failure so the allocated NAT hook data is released only after an RCU grace period, avoiding use-after-free if the structures may still be accessed by readers. It preserves safe teardown semantics for RCU-protected objects during failed registration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer freeing nat_ops with RCU to avoid use-after-free during NAT hook unregistration.
intent_record.what: In nf_nat_unregister_fn(), the cleanup of nat_ops changed from a direct kfree(nat_ops) to kfree_rcu(nat_ops, rcu) while leaving the surrounding logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: The freed nat_ops object is now released after an RCU grace period instead of immediately, preventing readers that may still be accessing it under RCU from dereferencing freed memory and reducing the risk of use-after-free bugs.

grouping_result.intent: Defer freeing nat_ops with RCU to avoid use-after-free during NAT hook unregistration.

consistency_review.core_intent: Defer freeing NAT hook lookup/ops data with RCU in registration or unregister cleanup paths to prevent use-after-free races.
